predecessors.name: Livonian Brothers of the Sword
predecessors.text: the Bishopric of Dorpat: Tartu, Põlva, Võru and Jõgeva counties, as the page names them

successors.name: Tsardom of Russia
successors.text: the Bishopric of Dorpat: Tartu, Põlva, Võru and Jõgeva counties, as the page names them

ledger.x: 1224: the bishopric takes Dorpat as its centre.
22 January 1558: Ivan IV invades Livonia ('On 22 January 1558, Ivan reacted with the invasion of Livonia'); Dorpat falls in the same year.
1558: Dorpat taken; the contest ends with the bishopric's fall.
1558: the bishopric ceases to exist with the conquest of Tartu.

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: Russian troops took Dorpat in 1558 and the bishopric ceased to exist; the weakened Livonian Order was dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561.

certainty.note: The page names the four counties only; the Estonian county borders stand for the bishopric's boundary.
